title: This AI Funnel Scaled My SaaS to $7M/yr (Copy This)
speakers_and_attribution: The transcript appears to be a single Adam Robinson monologue, identified contextually through first-person references to RB2B, Retention.com and his personal content. Captions are not diarized; attribution is contextual rather than independently voice-verified. Named colleagues, contractors and co-hosts are discussed but do not speak. All business results are Adam's unverified self-reports.
summary: Adam describes RB2B's founder-led acquisition and conversion funnel: LinkedIn content, supporting acquisition channels, a weekly show and newsletter, free product access, automated upgrades, and separate AI systems for presales and support. He credits documentation and daily human supervision for improving AI support. He preserves direct calls with selected higher-paying customers for product learning. Reported efficiency coexists with substantial customer churn, and the closing arithmetic does not independently explain the claimed $7 million ARR.

key_learnings.claim: Adam describes an operating model in which systems handle repetitive customer interactions while humans improve those systems.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: This describes his chosen model; the claim that RB2B is exceptionally efficient is opinion, without comparative operating data.

key_learnings.claim: LinkedIn is RB2B's acquisition foundation because its intended buyers—B2B SaaS founders, marketers and salespeople—already spend time there. Adam attributes resonance to sharing operating problems such as layoffs, churn and failed strategies.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: Audience fit and transparency are his explanations for performance, not experimentally established causes. Captions are garbled around 00:01:46–00:01:50.

key_learnings.claim: RB2B supplements LinkedIn with cold email, retargeting, SEO and YouTube. Its outbound includes both cold prospects and recently identified website visitors; Adam links the strongest cited email result to recent visitor intent.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: The high conversion example belongs to one campaign involving recent visitors; it should not be generalized to all cold outbound.

key_learnings.claim: The paid advertising strategy targets people already familiar with Adam or RB2B through website visits or content engagement. SEO is presented as a slower channel whose results compound.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: Reported ad performance concerns retargeting, not cold acquisition. The transcript does not establish incremental attribution or SEO measurement definitions.

key_learnings.claim: Adam extends existing LinkedIn ideas into YouTube through a delegated workflow: maintain an ideas document, have a collaborator select topics and script from existing content, record, then delegate editing.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: His stated time commitment covers his own work, not the collaborator's labor. The collaborator's name is captioned as Samu.

key_learnings.claim: The weekly live show combines community, recurring audience contact, practical founder education and opportunities for guests to generate demos. LinkedIn and the newsletter distribute the show.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: These are intended functions; the transcript supplies attendance figures but no attributable revenue or demo totals.

key_learnings.claim: The newsletter and LinkedIn form a distribution loop: free product signups become newsletter subscribers, the newsletter republishes the previous week's strongest LinkedIn post, and readers return to its comments, potentially generating more reach and product signups.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: Adam describes the mechanism and expected reinforcement; the transcript does not quantify each transition.

key_learnings.claim: RB2B uses its own visitor-identification product to follow up with people who browse without submitting forms, making internal product use part of its acquisition process.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: The product capability and speed claims are promotional self-reports. No match-rate, eligibility or coverage evidence is supplied.

key_learnings.claim: A presales AI clone trained on Adam's content and RB2B knowledge is intended to answer common questions while serving visitors who specifically want access to the founder.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: Adam explicitly frames this as suitable for an influencer-led business. Claims that it answers as he would are not supported by accuracy or conversion evaluations. Tool name is captioned as Deli AI.

key_learnings.claim: A free tier without a credit-card requirement lets prospects experience visitor identification before paying. Traffic and credit limits then create a self-service upgrade path, with AI answering questions and no sales team calling to push upgrades.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: Adam links conversion quality to an audience already familiar with him and the product. This is not evidence that the same free-tier design would work with unqualified traffic.

key_learnings.claim: RB2B separates presales AI from post-signup support AI. Adam prefers the latter for support because it can access account-specific information such as plan, credit usage and account status.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: The tool is captioned as Intercom Finn. The example of using 147 of 150 credits is illustrative, not a reported customer outcome.

key_learnings.claim: Adam attributes improved AI ticket resolution to meticulous documentation: FAQs, troubleshooting guides and changelogs. A head of AI reviews tickets daily and corrects underlying content when answers are wrong.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: The before-and-after improvement is self-reported, with no dates, quality audit or evidence isolating documentation from other changes.

key_learnings.claim: Adam retains personal customer calls for learning about value, frustrations and what to build next. He prioritizes selected higher-paying customers and says he will not fully automate those relationships.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: His belief that the highest-paying customers provide the most valuable feedback is a prioritization judgment. This sample may not represent free users or lower-paying customers.

key_learnings.claim: High gross paid acquisition can conceal modest net customer growth. Adam identifies cancellations as RB2B's worst business problem even while presenting the overall operation as highly efficient.
key_learnings.speaker: Adam Robinson
key_learnings.caveat: He supplies customer counts rather than a churn percentage or revenue-retention figures. The closing ARR arithmetic requires reconciliation.

backstory_and_values.caveat: Company name is captioned as Robbley and needs verification. No exit date, ownership share or personal proceeds are stated.

backstory_and_values.speaker: Adam Robinson

metrics_and_dates.claim: Adam claims that sustaining the described net customer growth for 23 months produces a $7 million ARR business with two customer-facing employees.
metrics_and_dates.speaker: Adam Robinson
metrics_and_dates.caveat: The 23 months appear in a retrospective growth explanation but do not establish an exact launch date. The stated customer and pricing arithmetic does not independently reconcile to $7 million ARR.

tensions_and_corrections: Closing arithmetic: 50 net new customers per month for 23 months equals 1,150 customers. At the stated $230 monthly average, that implies $3.174 million ARR if starting from zero with constant pricing and growth. This does not reconcile to $7 million without additional information about starting customers, historical growth, pricing, expansion or other revenue. Preserve both reported figures.
The title says $7M/yr, while the closing spoken claim specifies $7 million ARR. Treat this as a recurring revenue run rate, not established annual recognized revenue, profit or cash.

Two customer-facing employees does not mean a two-person company. Adam also names content, outbound, advertising, SEO and AI collaborators; their FTE, contractor and shared-support arrangements and costs are unspecified.
The opening 85% AI-handled customer-interaction figure and later over-80% support-ticket resolution figure concern different stated scopes. Their denominators and relationship are not supplied.
The general claim that 97% of visitors take no action would conflict with a 6.6% signup rate if applied to the same population and period. The transcript does not establish that shared scope.
Traffic is described first as unique sessions and later as visitors. Presales AI volume is described as both questions and conversations. Preserve these measurement ambiguities.
High email conversion and advertising click-through rates are tied to recent visitors or retargeted audiences; they should not be reused as cold-audience benchmarks.
The efficiency narrative includes significant unresolved churn, and Adam explicitly preserves direct customer learning as a human activity.

Automatic captions include uncertain names and phrases, including Robbley, Taylor Harren, Samu, Deli AI, Intercom Finn, Beehive and the founders/$68 signup sentence. These require verification before precise reuse.
No explicit change of mind about bootstrapping versus VC is presented. The support-resolution improvement is an operational change, not evidence of a broader ideological reversal.
